sources.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (December 1997), 238 PDF pages
sources.locator: Ch. 1 'Special Relativity' printed pp. 28-31 (PDF pp. 35-38): energy-momentum tensors of dust, perfect fluids and a scalar field. Ch. 2 'Manifolds' printed pp. 48-54 (PDF pp. 55-61): canonical form of a Lorentzian form at a point, tensor densities and the volume element (2.44) as an n-form. Ch. 3 'Curvature' printed pp. 70-71 (PDF pp. 77-78): the variation of the proper-time functional; printed pp. 74-96 (PDF pp. 81-103) for heading-level scope of the curvature chapter. Ch. 4 'Gravitation' printed pp. 113-120 (PDF pp. 120-127): the field equations, the Hilbert action and the energy-momentum tensor; Ch. 5 printed pp. 140-142 (PDF pp. 147-149): isometries and Killing vectors (5.39)-(5.42).

contents.name: Ch. 1 (1.104)-(1.106) pp. 28-29: the energy-momentum tensor of dust, T^{mu nu} = rho U^mu U^nu, and its conservation
contents.support: The source tensor and conservation laws are the form restated as the dust model and, with pressure, as the perfect-fluid model; the equivalence with the divergence identity is proved in the paired proposition.

contents.name: Ch. 1 (1.107)-(1.110) pp. 29-30: the perfect-fluid tensor T^{mu nu} = (rho + p) U^mu U^nu + p eta^{mu nu} and its nonrelativistic reading
contents.support: The source tensor is restated with rest energy density, pressure and unit four-velocity; the source's conservation laws are the fluid equations of the definition.

contents.name: Ch. 2 pp. 48-51: the classification of quadratic forms and the canonical form of the metric at a point
contents.support: The lemma absorbs the source argument: an explicit maximum-entry bound on the perturbation, Sylvester's law and a finite-cover compactness argument make the local statement uniform on compactly supported perturbations.

contents.name: Ch. 2 pp. 49-54: transformation of the metric components, tensor densities and the volume element (2.44) as an n-form
contents.support: The determinant and density transformation laws of clause (a) are proved from the covariant transformation law and the multiplicativity of the determinant; the source's displayed formulas are the same identities.

contents.name: Ch. 2 pp. 52-54: the volume element sqrt|g| dx^0 wedge ... as an n-form and the integration measure
contents.support: The metric volume density w = sqrt|det g| and the local volume form are the definition's clause (a); the source's integration measure is the chart reading recorded there.

contents.name: Ch. 3 (3.48)-(3.53) pp. 70-71: the variation of the proper-time functional and the resulting geodesic equation
contents.support: Clause (f) restates the first-variation formulas of the standalone proper-time lemma in the same chart, C^2, fixed-endpoint hypotheses and adds the particle-action reading S_p = -mc times length.

contents.name: Ch. 5 (5.39)-(5.42) pp. 140-142: isometries and Killing vectors, L_X g_{mu nu} = 0 and the equivalent condition nabla_mu X_nu + nabla_nu X_mu = 0, with conserved quantities along geodesics
contents.support: The definition fixes the Lie-derivative form and records that the symmetrized-derivative equivalence is proved (not asserted) in the Killing theorem clause (a), matching the source's two forms.

contents.name: Ch. 4 (4.52) p. 113 and (4.74) p. 119: Einstein's equations, with and without a cosmological constant
contents.support: The direct-equation postulate adopts exactly the displayed equation G_ab + Lambda g_ab = kappa T_ab with Lambda a constant parameter, and carries the framework's unit conventions.

contents.name: Ch. 4 (4.54)-(4.67) pp. 115-117: the Hilbert action, the variation of the Ricci tensor and of the determinant, and the removal of the total-divergence term
contents.support: Clauses (b)-(e) prove the Palatini identity, the density variation and the chart-action variation with the divergence term integrated away under compact support, which is the source computation made precise.

contents.name: Ch. 4 (4.68)-(4.70) pp. 117-118: the total action, the definition T_{mu nu} = -(1/sqrt(-g)) delta S_M/delta g^{mu nu} and the coupled field equations
contents.support: The Hilbert tensor is defined by the metric-variation identity in the framework's units; the action-to-equation identification is proved in the paired physics theorem.

contents.name: Ch. 4 pp. 117-118: conservation of the energy-momentum tensor and its flux interpretation
contents.support: Necessary conservation is derived from the contracted Bianchi identity in clause (a); the flux reading is carried by the density-divergence theorem and the worked flux examples.

contents.name: Ch. 4 (4.72)-(4.73) p. 118: the Weak Energy Condition and its perfect-fluid specialization
contents.support: The counterexample uses exactly the pointwise WEC inequality of the source and exhibits a WEC tensor with nonzero divergence, refuting the implication from the condition alone.

contents.name: Ch. 4 pp. 119-120: the cosmological-constant discussion and the vacuum-energy reading of the Lambda term (4.74)-(4.76)
contents.reason: The cosmological models and the vacuum-energy interpretation are developed on the homogeneous-cosmology page; this pair adopts Lambda only as a constant parameter of the field law and makes no interpretive claim.

contents.name: Ch. 5-7 solution-and-application material (Schwarzschild geometry, gravitational waves and the weak-field/ADM developments)
contents.reason: Solution families and asymptotic energy constructions require the boundary and asymptotic machinery owned by the later GR pages of this run; this pair fixes only the field law, its consistency conditions and the local matter sectors.

sources.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), 125 PDF pages
sources.locator: Section 2.1 printed pp. 25-28 (PDF pp. 26-29): Lorentzian signature and the local normal form. Section 2.4 printed pp. 28-29 (PDF pp. 29-30): curves of extremal proper time. Section 5.3 printed pp. 53-56 (PDF pp. 54-57): Lie derivative, isometries and Killing's equation (5.20)-(5.23). Section 6.2 printed pp. 60-63 (PDF pp. 61-64): physical laws in curved spacetime. Section 6.4 printed pp. 66-69 (PDF pp. 67-70): the postulates of general relativity. Sections 8.6-8.7 printed pp. 108-110 (PDF pp. 109-111): integration on manifolds and Stokes' theorem. Sections 9.1-9.3 printed pp. 111-118 (PDF pp. 112-119): the Einstein-Hilbert and matter actions, their variations, the definition of T^{ab} and its conservation.

contents.name: Sec. 2.1 pp. 25-28: the signature of a Lorentzian metric and the local normal form g = diag(-1,1,1,1) at a point
contents.support: The lemma turns the source's normal-form statement into a quantitative openness statement (maximum-entry bound 1/8) and makes it uniform on compact support in finitely many charts.

contents.name: Sec. 2.4 pp. 28-29: curves of extremal proper time and the geodesic equation
contents.support: Clause (f) quotes the first-variation formulas and the stationarity characterization D_t gamma' = 0 under the chart, C^2, fixed-endpoint, timelike-fibre hypotheses.

contents.name: Secs. 8.6-8.7 pp. 108-110: integration on manifolds and Stokes' theorem; Sec. 9.2 pp. 111-115: the divergence theorem applied to action variations
contents.support: Clauses (a)-(c) prove the density-divergence identity, the Stokes flux balance with the side term -Phi_J(B) and the non-null face formula; the flat counterpart is worked on the examples page.

contents.name: Sec. 8.6 pp. 108-109: the volume element and integration on an oriented manifold
contents.support: The definition fixes vol_g = w dx^0 wedge ... wedge dx^3 chartwise, proved chart-independent, with the orientation as an independent datum.

contents.name: Sec. 6.2 (6.30)-(6.31) pp. 65-66: the perfect-fluid energy-momentum tensor, the conservation equations and the pressureless case
contents.support: The proposition proves the exact equivalence of nabla^a T_ab = 0 with the continuity/Euler equations and, for p = 0, with the dust system used by the dust definition.

contents.name: Sec. 6.4 pp. 66-69, postulates of general relativity: the symmetric conserved tensor T_ab (postulate 3) and G_ab = 8 pi G T_ab (postulate 4)
contents.support: The direct-equation postulate adopts the displayed equation with the framework's kappa = 8 pi G_N / c^4 and states the smooth-branch exclusions; the conservation condition is derived, not re-adopted.

contents.name: Sec. 5.3 pp. 53-56: the Lie derivative, Killing's equation (5.21)-(5.22) and the conservation of X_a V^a along geodesics
contents.support: The definition adopts the Lie-derivative characterization; the geodesic-contraction conservation is proved in clause (b) of the Killing theorem and worked on the examples page.

contents.name: Sec. 9.1-9.2 (9.2)-(9.6) and (9.21)-(9.25) pp. 111-115: the scalar-field action, its equation of motion and the variation of the Einstein-Hilbert action
contents.support:
Current local carrier Definition scope for owner source-coverage reconciliation:

Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]), let $c>0$ be a fixed
real constant, and let $\nabla$ be the metric-selected connection of $g$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]).

**(a) Data.** A **scalar-field matter model** on $M$ is a triple
$(\varphi,V,K)$ consisting of

- a smooth function $\varphi:M\to\mathbb R$
  ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]], with target the
  standard one-dimensional smooth manifold $\mathbb R$);
- a smooth function $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, the **potential**; and
- a real constant $K>0$, the **coupling**.

The physical reading of $K$ and of the units of $\varphi$ and $V$ is fixed by
the framework's matter postulate, not by this definition.

**(b) Scalar-action density and action differences.** For every smooth
function $\varphi'$ and every smooth Lorentzian metric $g'$ of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ on $M$ define the **scalar-action density**

$$\ell(\varphi',g'):=-\frac{K}{c}\Bigl[\tfrac12\,g'^{ab}\,\partial_a\varphi'\, \partial_b\varphi'+V(\varphi')\Bigr]\mathrm{vol}_{g'}\in\Omega^4(M),$$

where $g'^{ab}$ are the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]) and
$\mathrm{vol}_{g'}$ the metric volume form
([[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]). For two pairs $(\varphi,g)$
and $(\varphi',g')$ with $\varphi'-\varphi$ and all components of $g'-g$
supported in a compact set, the difference $\ell(\varphi',g')-\ell(\varphi,g)$
is a compactly supported smooth $4$-form and the **action difference**

$$\Delta S:=\int_M\bigl[\ell(\varphi',g')-\ell(\varphi,g)\bigr]$$

is a real number ([[lem-finite-chart-localization-defines-choice-free-integration-and-compact-stokes]]),
the integral being independent of how the pair $(\varphi,g)$ is extended outside
the support. Only such differences are used; no integrality of the total
action on a noncompact $M$ is asserted.

**(c) Scalar equation and candidate stress-energy tensor.** The model's
**scalar equation of motion** is

$$\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0,\qquad \Box_g\varphi:=\nabla^a\partial_a\varphi,$$

and the model's **candidate stress-energy tensor** is the smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field

$$T_{ab}:=K\Bigl[\partial_a\varphi\,\partial_b\varphi -g_{ab}\Bigl(\tfrac12\,\partial^c\varphi\,\partial_c\varphi+V(\varphi)\Bigr)\Bigr],$$

with $\partial^c\varphi\,\partial_c\varphi=g^{cd}\partial_c\varphi\,
\partial_d\varphi$ ([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). That this candidate is indeed
the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the model, and that the scalar equation implies its conservation, are proved in
[[prop-gr-scalar-field-stress-energy-conservation]]; the definition itself
asserts neither proved property, and this item does not assert that any solution of
the scalar equation exists.

Exact local scope projection only; authoritative source fidelity and full consumer acceptance remain GR owner duties.

contents.name: Sec. 9.3 (9.28)-(9.29) p. 116: the definition T^{ab} = (2/sqrt(-g)) delta S_matter/delta g_{ab}
contents.support: The Hilbert tensor is defined by the equivalent contravariant-variation identity with the library sign convention and the 1/(2c) normalization, matching the framework's coupling;

contents.name: Sec. 9.3 (9.31)-(9.32) p. 116: the scalar-field energy-momentum tensor and its divergence identity
contents.support:
Current local carrier Statement scope for owner source-coverage reconciliation:

Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and let $(\varphi,V,K)$ be a scalar-field
matter model on $M$ with action differences $\Delta S$, scalar equation
$\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0$ and candidate stress-energy tensor $T$
([[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]],
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]).

**(a) Matter first variation.** Let $u\mapsto\varphi_u$, $|u|<u_0$, be a family
of smooth functions with $\varphi_{u=0}=\varphi$ such that $(\varphi_u-\varphi)$ is supported in a fixed
compact set for all $u$ and the functions $(u,p)\mapsto\varphi_u(p)$ are
smooth. Then $u\mapsto\Delta S(\varphi_u,g)$ is differentiable at $0$ and

$$\frac{d}{du}\Big|_{u=0}\Delta S(\varphi_u,g)=\frac{K}{c}\int_M\bigl(\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)\bigr)\,\delta\varphi\,\mathrm{vol}_g,\qquad \delta\varphi:=\partial_u\varphi_u|_{u=0}.$$

In particular the family is stationary in this direction, for every such
family, exactly when $\Box_g\varphi=V'(\varphi)$.

**(b) Metric variation and Hilbert tensor.** Let $s\mapsto g_s$, $|s|<s_0$, be
a smooth metric family at $g$ with compactly supported variation, and let
$q^{ab}=\partial_sg_s^{ab}|_{s=0}$. Then

$$\frac{d}{ds}\Big|_{s=0}\Delta S(\varphi,g_s)=-\frac{1}{2c}\int_M T_{ab}\,q^{ab}\,\mathrm{vol}_g .$$

Consequently $T$ is the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the scalar-field model
at $(g,\varphi)$ with respect to $c$
([[def-gr-hilbert-stress-energy-tensor]]), and by
[[lem-gr-hilbert-tensor-uniqueness]] it is the only one.

**(c) Conservation identity.** On $M$,

$$\nabla^aT_{ab}=K\bigl(\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)\bigr)\partial_b\varphi .$$

Consequently the scalar equation implies $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$. Conversely conservation implies the scalar equation at each point where $d\varphi\ne0$, and therefore everywhere if that set is dense, by continuity. No converse follows on an open constant-field region.

Exact local scope projection only; authoritative source fidelity and full consumer acceptance remain GR owner duties.

contents.name: Sec. 9.3 (9.35)-(9.41) pp. 117-118: conservation of T^{ab} from diffeomorphism invariance of the matter action
contents.support: Clause (d) isolates the four hypotheses (H1)-(H4) that make the source's diffeomorphism argument a complete conditional deduction, including the compact-support completeness input.

contents.name: Sec. 9.2 (9.23)-(9.25) pp. 114-116: the compactly supported variation hypothesis for the Einstein-Hilbert action and the boundary-variation case not treated
contents.reason: The framework's postulates adopt no boundary terms, so nonzero metric variations on a boundary, junction conditions and their surface terms require mathematics and assumptions this page deliberately does not supply.

contents.name: Sec. 6.4 postulate 2 pp. 66-69 and the equivalence-principle/free-fall material
contents.reason: The free-fall and equivalence-principle postulates are adopted and developed on the connections-and-free-fall page of this run; this pair consumes their consequences but does not rebuild them.

sources.title: D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), 289 PDF pages
sources.locator: Section 1.2.1 printed pp. 12-16 (PDF pp. 19-23): the relativistic particle action and its Euler-Lagrange equation. Section 3.4.1 printed pp. 130-132 (PDF pp. 137-139): the contracted Bianchi identity and the Einstein tensor. Section 4.1 printed pp. 140-144 (PDF pp. 147-151): the Einstein-Hilbert action with cosmological constant and its variation. Sections 4.3-4.5 printed pp. 159-198 (PDF pp. 166-205): symmetries and Killing vectors, the field equations with matter, the scalar, dust and perfect-fluid sectors, charge conservation with figures 40-41 and the energy conditions, itemized below.

contents.name: Sec. 1.2.1 pp. 12-16: the particle action and the resulting Euler-Lagrange/geodesic equation
contents.support: Clause (f) relates S_p to the length functional and derives stationarity exactly when D_t gamma' = 0, under the restricted curve class of the standalone lemma.

contents.name: Sec. 4.3 pp. 159-162: isometries, Killing's equation and the conserved quantity built from a Killing vector
contents.support: Clause (b) proves the constant contraction along geodesics and clause (c) the conserved current from a divergence-free symmetric tensor and a Killing field.

contents.name: Sec. 4.1 pp. 140-142: the variation of sqrt(-g) and of the Einstein-Hilbert action (delta sqrt(-g) and the Palatini identity)
contents.support: The lemma proves partial_a w = (1/2) w g^{bc} partial_a g_{bc} and the Christoffel-trace identity that the source uses, so the density variation is available from this page.

contents.name: Sec. 4.1 pp. 141-144: the Einstein-Hilbert action with cosmological constant and its variation giving the combined field equations (4.47)
contents.support: The physics theorem proves the equivalence between stationarity of the total action difference and G_ab + Lambda g_ab = kappa T_ab with the framework's coupling, using the compactly supported variation class.

contents.name: Secs. 4.5.1 and 4.5.3 pp. 180-185: the free scalar field action, its wave equation and its energy-momentum tensor (4.51)

contents.name: Sec. 4.5.2 pp. 182-183: the definition (4.46) T_{mu nu} = -(2/sqrt(-g)) delta S_M/delta g^{mu nu} and the field equations with matter
contents.support: The definition records the variational convention and proves uniqueness of the tensor; the normalization matches kappa = 8 pi G_N/c^4 and the Einstein-Hilbert prefactor.

contents.name: Sec. 4.5.3 pp. 183-185: conservation of the energy-momentum tensor from diffeomorphism invariance
contents.support: Clause (d) proves nabla^a T_ab = 0 from the stated invariance and on-shell hypotheses and records the inherited AC_omega completeness assumption of the flow argument.

contents.name: Sec. 4.5.4 pp. 185-187: the dust and perfect-fluid energy-momentum tensors (4.53) and the conservation equations (4.54)-(4.55)
contents.support: The proposition proves both equivalences between the divergence-free condition and the dust system / fluid equations, including the role of rho > 0 in the converse.

contents.name: Sec. 4.5.5 pp. 187-191 and figures 40-41: charge conservation in curved spacetime, the flux through the timelike boundary B and Q(Sigma_2) = Q(Sigma_1) when no current flows out
contents.support: The example computes a divergence-free current with nonzero side flux density, exercising exactly the side-flux term of the balance; the counterexample shows a single face flux need not vanish.

contents.name: Sec. 4.5.7 pp. 194-198: the energy conditions and their perfect-fluid specializations including the cosmological case
contents.support: Clause (f) proves the four rest-frame equivalences (WEC, NEC, DEC, SEC) from the tensor form; the examples page evaluates dust, radiation and both signs of the effective cosmological fluid.

contents.name: Sec. 3.4.1 pp. 130-132: the contracted Bianchi identity and the trace of the field equations
contents.support: Clauses (a)-(c) derive necessary conservation, the trace identity -S + 4 Lambda = kappa tr T and the nonconstant-Lambda identity kappa nabla^a T_ab = partial_b Lambda.
